text.p: Programme of soccer matches in the German league championship on Tuesday and Wednesday (league positions in brackets):

Karlsruhe are getting used to life without midfield mainstay Thomas Haessler after he broke his leg shortly after recovering from a complex ankle fracture. But the absence of midfielder Michael Tarnat and league top scorer Sean Dundee will be severe handicaps for Winfried Schaefer's team, even against a Bochum side which has not won in five matches.

Bremen need to shake off the memory of Saturday's 4-1 defeat at relegation-threatened Borussia Moenchengladbach but field a full-strength side to entertain St Pauli. The Hamburg side look increasingly like relegation candidates after losing four and drawing one of their last five games but club president Heinz Wiesener says coach Uli Maslo "has proved that he can keep this team in the first division".

Moenchengladbach have won two and drawn two since the winter break under new trainer Hannes Bongartz, with Polish striker Andrzej Juskowiak finally finding the net. While captain Stefan Effenberg is under a cloud amid accusations that he beat a drunk outside his home, Hamburg's troubles are greater. Coach Felix Magath has made clear midfielder Markus Schupp will not play for him again after criticising Magath's tough training regime in public. Karsten Baeron, Jakob Friis-Hansen and Bernd Hollerbach will all be missing for Hamburg but defender Stephane Henchoz and midfielder Sven Kmetsch return from suspension.

Schalke have not lost nor conceded a goal in eight games and are challenging strongly for a UEFA Cup place. Only goal difference is keeping them out of fifth place and they should improve matters against low-scoring Duisburg who have not won in four matches since the winter break.

Stuttgart returned to winning ways by firing four past Hamburg at the weekend, and need to prove that the "magic triangle" up front of Fredi Bobic, Giovane Elber and Krasimir Balakov really have got the club's title challenge back on the rails. Cologne have faded from a bright start to the season and should be no match for an in-form Stuttgart.

Victory is a must for the reigning champions who returned to the top of the table as Bayern Munich came unstuck last weekend. After beating Freiburg thanks to a controversial penalty, Dortmund will want to show they need no luck this time.

Duesseldorf have a surprisingly good home record including, recently, a 4-1 defeat of Bremen and a shock 2-0 victory over Dortmund. Freiburg look doomed to relegation. They will be without Dutch striker Harry Decheiver, whose goals helped to save them from relegation last year but who has now alienated coach and fellow players alike and is set to be sold.

Leverkusen will be buoyant after thumping Bayern Munich 5-2 and re-establishing themselves as title candidates, even without the services of first-choice strikers Ulf Kirsten and Eric Meijer. Hat-trick hero Markus Feldhoff hopes to keep his place in the side against an erratic 1860 side who brushed aside Fortuna Duesseldorf 3-0 last week.

Bielefeld have won four of their last five games but are up against a side who are likely to be working off their frustration after Sunday's drubbing by Leverkusen. Bayern need to eliminate their occasional large-scale defensive lapses and improve their motivation. But they have lost only twice in the league this season and should come away with at least a point.
